candidate.answerReason: Every 12 disks cost $15 and bring in $20, earning $5. Twenty such batches earn $100 and contain 240 disks.

methods.label: Compare batches of twelve
methods.explanation:
Using the same number of disks for buying and selling makes the profit easy to compare. The smallest batch that contains whole groups of both \(4\) and \(3\) disks has \(12\) disks.

Buying \(12\) disks costs \(3\cdot\$5=\$15\), while selling them brings in \(4\cdot\$5=\$20\). The profit is therefore \(\$20-\$15=\$5\) per batch. Since both cost and revenue scale with the number of disks, earning \(\$100\) requires \(100\div5=20\) such batches. The number of disks is
\[
20\cdot12=\boxed{240},
\]
choice \(\boxed{\text{D}}\).
